question: Estimate the time it takes to send \(60\) blocks of data over a communications channel if each block consists of \(512\) “chunks” and the channel can transmit \(120\) chunks per second.
solution:
First count the chunks in all \(60\) blocks. Then divide by the number of chunks transmitted each second to find the time in seconds:
\[
\text{time}=\frac{60\cdot512}{120}=256\text{ seconds}.
\]
Since \(1\) minute is \(60\) seconds and
\[
256=4\cdot60+16,
\]
the exact time is \(4\) minutes \(16\) seconds. This is approximately \(\boxed{4\text{ minutes}}\), choice \(\text{D}\).

nodes.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions , including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units. For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction 1/2/1/4 miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour.
